newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Wednesday following overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 24,000 yuan ($2,892) per tonne, losing 50 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 23,920 and hit a high of 24,010.
April rose 30 to 23,530, May fell 70 to 23,620, June 60 to 23,820, August 80 to 23,990 and September 170 to 23,900.
Combined volume fell to 24,610 tonnes from 26,840.

Copper opened lower on LME losses but short-covering pushed the prices up from their lows during the rest of the session, traders said, adding copper was still consolidating in a narrow range with the market trend unclear.

"Most investors do not think copper will fall sharply, so there was little selling at low levels," one trader said. "Retail investors looking for quick profits dominated the day's trading while most institutions stayed on the sidelines."
Traders said investors were mixed about the future market trend but sharp fluctuations were unlikely in the absence of market-moving news.
Aluminium ended down. April fell 130 yuan to 16,020 yuan per tonne, May 150 to 16,250, June 220 to 16,530 and July 150 to 16,700.
Combined volume rose to 1,580 tonnes from 710.
